criteria.justification: The response explicitly diagnoses “a process failure presenting as a naming failure” and says the recurring issue is that “any name can be defeated,” rather than treating round four as another search for the perfect label.

It proposes a named decider, required approver, deadline, agreed closing condition, and reopening only for genuinely new information. It also explicitly states that the costs of another cycle now exceed the cost of accepting a slightly imperfect name.

The response acknowledges that prior objections were valid but creates a rule that the decision may reopen only for “new information…not on a new opinion,” using pre-ranked criteria to prevent lower-priority tradeoffs from triggering repeated re-litigation.

It treats the locked API field and product-family consistency as hard constraints, proposing a customer-facing name that “doesn't fight the locked API field” rather than attempting to reopen the underlying architecture.

Rather than inventing another ad hoc candidate, it proposes ranked criteria, contextual explanatory copy, comparative testing, and reuse of a prior option where appropriate. It clearly explains that this differs from prior isolated validation because it selects the least-confusing acceptable option under agreed decision rules.
